Fred White, who was making his last appearance for the Club owing to his being called for the R.A.F., finished 2nd. The field events men—Syd Jones and Bill Sutton—gained full points in most of the field events. Charlie Jones also scored in these events.
Sid Jones was again the outstanding Weight Putter and Discus man. He was consistently doing over 38 feet and his best performance was over 40 feet in the Weight.
Botwright, Bill Bowers, Sid.
Bill Sutton was second in the Weight and also gained third place in the Discus, but Bill seems to miss the support of Syd Jones, our other " strong " man, who is in the Services.

It was impossible to include more field events as there were no jumping pits on the ground, and the other displays prevented a Javelin or Discus event being held. We were very glad to welcome Syd Jones in the Weight, and he won with a fine put of 38ft. 11in.

Both Syd Jones and Laurie Jackson also helped us when on leave. Sid Jones, our weight slinger, has gone out East, and more news is awaited. Charlie Redgrave, having passed his Dental Exams. at Chatham, has now been sent to Skegness.
Syd Jones, our weight putter, also arrived in the Middle East, with one stripe up. Dennis Rodaway, we understand, has been commissioned in the Fleet Air Arm.
Pat Ridge, our Irish Guardsman, won both the Weight Put and Discus Throw, and what a trio he, Syd Jones and Bill Sutton would make. We were without Melchior in the Javelin, but B.
Still making good progress and occasionally looks in at the Hall. Syd Jones airgraphs from the Middle East that he is still a signaller. The Editor must have mistaken Sgn. for Sgnt.

Sid Jones, writing from the M.E.F., says that he has competed in an International Sports meeting with Britain, New Zealand and S. Africa, and was most surprised at not meeting any other members there.

News has been received that Sid Jones, our Shot Putt Champion, who is a sapper in North Africa, was honoured by being selected to represent Great Britain in a match at Cairo against South Africa, New Zealand and Canada.
Syd Jones was home on leave during the summer.

In the middle of the season we were glad to see Sid Jones, our Shot Champion, home on leave from Germany. He was persuaded to turn out, and in spite of not being stripped, managed to get second place with an effort of 35 feet 8 ins., showing he has none of his powers impaired.
How many other Belgravians have saved the Army's petrol at the expense of their leather! Jim Heathfield, with the B.A.O.R., met Sid. Jones in Germany, and they had a long chat together.

We welcome the return of Sid Jones and Bill Sutton from the Forces and genial Jerry Thompson, after suffering from sugar diabetes, has been one of the features of the Section's activities during the past summer.
The field events saw the Police gaining most points, but Sid Jones, now out of the Army, showed some of his old form in the Shot Putt, and young Dick Negus won the High Jump.
Jones (5ft. 5in.), 3 S.
In the field events, our representatives had very little opposition, and with Charlie Melchior and Syd Jones, we gained maximum points in the Weight and Javelin events.

Charlie Jones was second in the Long Jump and our "heavy" brigade of Syd Jones and Bill Sutton gained useful points in the Weight Putt. Alan Dunn beat Charlie Melchior in the Javelin Throw in finishing second to Dalyrymple of L.A.C.

Syd Jones and Bill Sutton were first and second in the Weight, and Syd and Alan Dunn also gained major points in the Discus. Dick Negus was off form in the jumping events and is maybe feeling the effects of a very full season.

Jerry Thompson beat Syd Jones in the Weight Putt, although both men have done better performances during the season. So concluded our first post-war championship meeting, and we have every reason to be more than satisfied with the various results.

In the Field Events Syd Jones won the Weight with 38ft. 4in., and showed he is fast getting back to his pre-war performances. Syd also gained second place in the Discus, and it was the latter result that finally decided the match.
The Field Event handicaps were well supported and Bill Sutton and Syd Jones were among the prize-winners, and it was pleasing to see Laurie Jackson gaining a first award.
It was hoped that Sid Jones would return to his pre-war form in the Shot and Discus events, in this, his first full season after demobilisation.

Jock Mackenzie in the Discus should again show improvement and will be backed up by Sid Jones and Bill Sutton. Sid and Bill will be our Shot Putters, but Jock Mackenzie and Les Christmas have possibilities if they only get down to training.
